Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Free and Bound Occurrences of Variables
examples.problem:
$$
\big( \, \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\text{I}}}{x} \in \mathbb{R}, \, 
 {x} 
> 1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \exists 
{y} 
\in [0, 2\pi), \, 
\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\text{II}}}{x} \!
\cos\!\!{\underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[2pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\text{III}}}{y}} \!=1 \, \big)
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
examples.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{\small\text{b}})$ or free $(\bbox[2pt, LightBlue]{\small\text{f}}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is *bound* since it is placed right next to the quantifier $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall}{:}$

$$
\big( \,\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall} \!\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{x} \!\! \in \mathbb{R}, \,  x > 1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, 
{\exists} {y} 
\in [0, 2\pi), \, x\cos y =1\, \big)
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $x$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

- Occurrence III of the variable $y$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $\exists y$ that uses $y{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14100350/assets/0d50f5d97bd29abbe04f6cbe29385dced4b064c953aef34d41c1a96c0a6efd4f.png)

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
\big( \, {\forall} \!\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{x} \!\! \in \mathbb{R}, \,  \!\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{x} \!\! > 1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, 
{\exists} \!\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y} \!\!
\in [0, 2\pi), \, \!\! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{x} \!\! \cos \!\!\!\underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \[4pt] \uparrow \[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y}\! =1\, \big)
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "II only."

feedback.problem:
$\,$ $∀\,a,b\in Z,\,a+b\in Z.$

Which of the following expresses the statement given above?
feedback.worked_solution:
Our quantified statement reads as follows:

$\,$ **For all** $a\in Z$ and **for all** $b\in Z,$   $\,a+b\in Z.$

This can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ Every pair of integers has an integer sum.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: Every pair of integers has an integer sum.
